Under the hood: strategy, model and contrasts

Witold E. Wolski

2026-11-23

Source: vignettes/articles/LowLevelAPI.Rmd
LowLevelAPI.Rmd

Purpose

build_contrast_analysis() chains three steps:

  1. a strategy says which model to fit per protein, e.g. strategy_lm()
  2. build_model() fits it to every protein and returns a Model
  3. Contrasts computes the contrasts from the models; ContrastsModerated shrinks their variances with the empirical Bayes method

This article runs the steps by hand for the lm method. Use them to inspect the per-protein models, to change one step, or to add a new modelling backend. For analyses, use build_contrast_analysis().

library(prolfqua)
sim <- sim_lfq_data_protein_config(n_proteins = 100, seed = 1234)
lfq <- LFQData$new(sim$data, sim$config)
contrasts <- c(AvsC = "group_A - group_Ctrl", BvsC = "group_B - group_Ctrl")

The facade 

fa <- build_contrast_analysis(lfq, "~ group_", contrasts, method = "lm")

The same, step by step

The lm method weights each protein intensity by its number of peptides, the column lfq$nr_children_col().

strat <- strategy_lm(paste(lfq$response(), "~ group_"), weights = lfq$nr_children_col())
mod <- build_model(lfq, strat)
contr <- Contrasts$new(mod, contrasts, model_name = "lm")
contr_mod <- ContrastsModerated$new(contr)

Both give the same result:

by_facade <- dplyr::arrange(fa$get_contrasts(), protein_Id, contrast)
by_hand <- dplyr::arrange(contr_mod$get_contrasts(), protein_Id, contrast)
all.equal(by_facade$diff, by_hand$diff)
## [1] TRUE
all.equal(by_facade$p.value, by_hand$p.value)
## [1] TRUE

The facade keeps the intermediate objects, so you can also take them from there: fa$model is the Model, fa$contrast the moderated contrasts.

Inspecting the models

mod$model_df holds one row per protein with its fitted model and fit diagnostics.

mod$model_df |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, has_model_fit, isSingular, nr_coef_not_NA, sigma, df.residual) |>
  head()
## # A tibble: 6 × 6
## # Groups:   protein_Id [6]
##   protein_Id  has_model_fit isSingular nr_coef_not_NA sigma df.residual

From a formula to coefficient weights

setup_analysis() treats configured predictors as categorical labels. It converts numeric predictors and ordered factors to character too, so ordered levels and numeric slopes are not retained by that route. It builds the configured identifiers and retains the analysis columns; other columns and their attributes are discarded. The names in config$factors are the predictor names used in the formula. Method keys, predictor names and contrast names are case sensitive.

R normally uses treatment coding (options("contrasts")): an intercept for the reference group and one coefficient per other level. Character predictors are sorted, so here group_A is the reference. The design and the coefficients of the first protein:

fit <- mod$model_df$linear_model[[1]]
unique(model.matrix(fit))
##    (Intercept) group_B group_Ctrl
## 1            1       0          0
## 5            1       1          0
## 10           1       0          1
coef(fit)
## (Intercept)     group_B  group_Ctrl 
##   21.994705   -2.390970   -1.372319

A contrast string refers to group means, not to coefficients. Contrasts$get_linfct() shows the weights on the coefficients that each contrast becomes; the avg_ rows are the mean of the two groups compared. Because A is the reference, AvsC is minus the group_Ctrl coefficient. The weights times the coefficients give the estimates in get_contrasts():

weights <- contr$get_linfct()
weights
##          (Intercept) group_B group_Ctrl
## AvsC               0     0.0       -1.0
## BvsC               0     1.0       -1.0
## avg_AvsC           1     0.0        0.5
## avg_BvsC           1     0.5        0.5
drop(weights %*% coef(fit))
##      AvsC      BvsC  avg_AvsC  avg_BvsC 
##  1.372319 -1.018651 21.308545 20.113060
dplyr::filter(contr$get_contrasts(), protein_Id == mod$model_df$protein_Id[1])[, c("contrast", "diff")]
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   contrast  diff
##   <chr>    <dbl>
## 1 AvsC      1.37
## 2 BvsC     -1.02

If another level were the reference, the coefficients and the weights would change, but each contrast of group means would estimate the same difference.

Two factors and their interaction

~ Treatment * Background expands to ~ Treatment + Background + Treatment:Background. With two levels per factor its four columns are the intercept, the Treatment effect at the reference Background, the Background effect at the reference Treatment, and their interaction:

sim2 <- sim_lfq_data_2factor_config(n_proteins = 50, seed = 1234)
lfq2 <- LFQData$new(sim2$data, sim2$config)
mod2 <- build_model(lfq2, strategy_lm(paste(lfq2$response(), "~ Treatment * Background")))
fit2 <- mod2$model_df$linear_model[[1]]
unique(model.matrix(fit2))
##    (Intercept) TreatmentB BackgroundZ TreatmentB:BackgroundZ
## 1            1          0           0                      0
## 5            1          1           0                      0
## 9            1          1           1                      1
## 13           1          0           1                      0

A factor level such as TreatmentB stands for the mean over the cells with that level, each cell weighted equally; a cell such as `TreatmentB:BackgroundX` stands for one cell (quote cell names with backticks because they contain a colon). A contrast may refer to earlier contrasts by name, here to give the interaction: the change of the B-vs-A difference between the two backgrounds.

contrasts2 <- c(
  B_vs_A = "TreatmentB - TreatmentA",
  B_vs_A_at_X = "`TreatmentB:BackgroundX` - `TreatmentA:BackgroundX`",
  B_vs_A_at_Z = "`TreatmentB:BackgroundZ` - `TreatmentA:BackgroundZ`",
  interaction = "B_vs_A_at_Z - B_vs_A_at_X"
)
contr2 <- Contrasts$new(mod2, contrasts2, model_name = "lm")
weights2 <- contr2$get_linfct()
weights2[!startsWith(rownames(weights2), "avg_"), ]
##             (Intercept) TreatmentB BackgroundZ TreatmentB:BackgroundZ
## B_vs_A                0          1           0                    0.5
## B_vs_A_at_X           0          1           0                    0.0
## B_vs_A_at_Z           0          1           0                    1.0
## interaction           0          0           0                    1.0
drop(weights2 %*% coef(fit2))[names(contrasts2)]
##      B_vs_A B_vs_A_at_X B_vs_A_at_Z interaction 
##  -0.4088817  -2.1299824   1.3122189   3.4422013
dplyr::filter(contr2$get_contrasts(), protein_Id == mod2$model_df$protein_Id[1])[, c("contrast", "diff")]
## # A tibble: 4 × 2
##   contrast      diff
##   <chr>        <dbl>
## 1 B_vs_A      -0.409
## 2 B_vs_A_at_X -2.13 
## 3 B_vs_A_at_Z  1.31 
## 4 interaction  3.44

The weights assume categorical predictors and the usual intercept-based coding; they do not give marginal means for continuous covariates or other contrast codings. When a protein lacks a factor combination, a contrast that needs a coefficient the protein cannot estimate is NA for that protein; build_contrast_analysis() rejects a group that is absent from the whole dataset.

Without moderation

Contrasts alone gives the unmoderated contrasts, which the facades do not expose. Moderation stabilises the variances estimated from few observations:

data.frame(
  contrasts = c("Contrasts", "ContrastsModerated"),
  FDR_lt_0.1 = c(
    sum(contr$get_contrasts()$FDR < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(contr_mod$get_contrasts()$FDR < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)
##            contrasts FDR_lt_0.1
## 1          Contrasts         30
## 2 ContrastsModerated         33

Changing one step

Replace the strategy to fit another model per protein, e.g. a robust linear model with strategy_rlm(); the other steps stay the same.

mod_rlm <- build_model(lfq, strategy_rlm(paste(lfq$response(), "~ group_")))
contr_rlm <- ContrastsModerated$new(Contrasts$new(mod_rlm, contrasts, model_name = "rlm"))
head(contr_rlm$get_contrasts()[, c("protein_Id", "contrast", "diff", "p.value", "FDR")])
## # A tibble: 6 × 5
##   protein_Id  contrast    diff   p.value      FDR
##   <chr>       <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1 0EfVhX~3967 AvsC      1.27   0.0637    0.328   
## 2 0m5WN4~6025 AvsC     -3.04   0.0000345 0.000844
## 3 0YSKpy~2865 AvsC      0.144  0.829     0.985   
## 4 3QLHfm~8938 AvsC     -0.116  0.857     0.985   
## 5 3QYop0~7543 AvsC      0.0800 0.911     0.985   
## 6 76k03k~7094 AvsC      0.884  0.169     0.519

Adding a backend

A facade class wraps the steps of one method. register_facade() adds it to the registry, after which build_contrast_analysis(method = ...) finds it. list_facades() shows the registry:

names(list_facades())
##  [1] "binomial_firth_nested" "binomial_nested"       "deqms"                
##  [4] "deqms_voom"            "firth"                 "hurdle_nested"        
##  [7] "limma"                 "limma_impute"          "limma_voom"           
## [10] "limma_voom_impute"     "limpa"                 "limpa_nested"         
## [13] "lm"                    "lm_impute"             "lmer_nested"          
## [16] "rfit"                  "rfit_impute"           "rlm"                  
## [19] "ropeca_nested"         "ropecaV2_nested"
